data.name: Chapter 1: Test Rules
entries: This chapter introduces test mechanics for validation and LaTeX generation testing.
These rules are designed to exercise various rendering features without using copyrighted content.

entries.name: New Mechanics
entries: This section covers the basic test mechanics that form the foundation of the testing system.

entries.name: Core Test Rules
entries: Higher rolls are generally better for test outcomes.
Critical failures occur on a roll of 1, critical successes on 20.

entries.name: Test Design Philosophy
entries: When designing tests, consider both positive and negative cases.
Edge cases often reveal the most interesting bugs.
Always validate your assumptions with actual data.

entries.name: Advanced Testing Concepts
entries: This section covers more complex testing scenarios that might be encountered in real-world applications.

entries.name: Integration Testing
entries: Integration tests verify that multiple components work together correctly.
They are essential for catching issues that unit tests might miss.
However, they can be more complex to set up and maintain.

items: Test data should be realistic but not copyrighted
Edge cases are particularly important to test

data.name: Chapter 2: Implementation Guidelines
entries: Following established patterns makes code more maintainable and easier to understand.

entries.name: Best Practices
entries: This section outlines best practices for writing maintainable and effective test code.

entries.name: Code Quality
entries: Write clear, self-documenting code whenever possible.
Use meaningful variable and function names.
Keep functions focused on a single responsibility.
Add comments for complex logic, but prefer clear code over comments.
